description: Maps the input record onto the output channel's columns.
Writes the records of its input channel to partition files.
Aggregate the input records to a single output record
Analyze each columns of the input records, emit a record per column with various metrics to the output channel
Anonymize or de-identify input records using an analysis lookup identifying columns containing sensitive data.
Analyze selected column and send to output channel their top percentile values
Compute the correlation between sets of columns identified by classification via a lookup table.
Apply a filter to input records, sending retained records to the output channel. Cap the number of retained records if specified.
Filter the input records to retain a single record per composite key value, records sent to the output channel have a distinct composite key.

Shuffle data on a per-column basis for retained columns specified in a lookup. The number of input records is capped by configuration. The number of generated output records is also specified by configuration.
Group the input records into bundles using a composite key. Each output records correspond to a bundle where each element of the output record contains an input record.
Sort the input records in memory, send the sorted records to output channel.

Merge sorted records from multiple channels using a grouping composite key. All input channels must be sorted using the same logical sort order. Bundled records are sent to the output channel, each element of the output records correspond to an input record.

Input channel contains either individual or bundled input records. Each record or bundle are sent to JetRules as a rule session. Output records are extracted by type from the rule session, each type correspond to an output channel.
Calls the infer server once per record and augments the record in place with values extracted from the model response.
Reshapes records from one channel's columns onto another's: the mapping and staging theme.
Collapses many records to few: counts, sums and the group keys they are taken over.
Partial aggregations computed per shard in the map phase of a map_reduce column operator.
notes: Corpus-attested: distinct_count (6), sum (4), count (2). min/max/avrg added as the same kind of per-shard partial; no live instance attests them here. select/value/eval deliberately excluded - the corpus carries group keys in the hosting aggregate's own columns, never in a phase.

description: Operators that combine per-shard partial results in the reduce phase of a map_reduce column operator.
notes: Corpus-attested: count only (12 instances, no exceptions). sum/min/max added because they combine partials correctly. distinct_count and avrg deliberately excluded - neither composes across shards, which is likely why the corpus reduces distinct_count to a count.

description: Calls an inference server once per record and augments the record in place with values extracted from the model response, against whichever backend the deployment names.
notes: The backend-agnostic operator. Resolved into an ollama or vllm step by ResolveInferBackend before the validator runs, so this bundle describes what is authored rather than what is executed.

description: Calls a vLLM server's OpenAI-compatible api once per record and augments the record in place with values extracted from the model response, constraining generation to a schema when one is given.
notes: One of the two operators ResolveInferBackend rewrites an infer step into, so a document may name it directly or reach it through the backend the deployment sets. Unattested by the corpus: no live .pc.json carries a raw vllm step, so this bundle is authored on the operator's meaning and cannot be falsified by the corpus - the condition BUNDLES_SCHEMA.md records for clustering, arriving for a second reason.

description: Calls the infer server's embeddings endpoint once per record and writes the returned vector onto the record; builds a retrieval corpus rather than generating text.
notes: The third operator on the 15a inferBackend seam and the one that is not generative: no response_format, no think, and the vector reaches the record through vector_column rather than through a named response path. Corpus-attested in four files - the JetStore-owned embed_input_parts.pc.json installed into each of the four workspaces.

description: Renders one text template per record and augments the record in place with the rendered text.
notes: Added 2026-09-11 with the render token, on InferPipe's precedent: a bundle names exactly one TransformationSpec operator, so a new operator is a new bundle rather than a member of an existing one. columns_range is '-' because the operator runs no column transformations - it writes one column, named by render_config.output_column - which is the six-of-fifteen case the range table already records rather than a new one. No bundle_evidence.csv row, for the reason the three infer-family bundles have none: nothing regenerates that file.
